name: alpaca-ai-trading-agents-hackathon
note: Companion to knowledge-graph.md. Node types: platform, api, tool, environment, constraint, rule, capability, strategy, pattern, competitor, partner, opening. Edge types: provides, enables, requires, blocks, constrains, default_for, used_by, satisfies, implies.

nodes.label: Alpaca
facts: Programmable brokerage: you supply an API key, your app places orders.
Alpaca Securities LLC (FINRA/SIPC) for securities; Alpaca Crypto LLC (FinCEN MSB) for crypto.
Lead partner of the hackathon.

nodes.label: Trading API
facts: Paper base URL https://paper-api.alpaca.markets
Auth headers APCA-API-KEY-ID and APCA-API-SECRET-KEY
Every response carries X-Request-ID

nodes.label: Market Data API
facts: Host data.alpaca.markets, same for paper and live.
Option chain and snapshot endpoints live under /v1beta1/options/

nodes.label: Broker API
facts: Brokerage-as-a-service: trade on behalf of other accounts.
OUT OF SCOPE for this hackathon - different auth and endpoints.

nodes.label: Alpaca MCP Server
facts: 65 documented tools; README claims 90+ across toolsets.
FastMCP generated from Alpaca OpenAPI specs, MIT licensed.
stdio transport by default; streamable-http optional.
V2 is NOT backward compatible with V1.
Defaults to paper via ALPACA_PAPER_TRADE=true.

nodes.label: Alpaca CLI
facts: brew install alpacahq/tap/cli
JSON default output; --csv, --jq, --quiet, --dry-run, --schema.
Exit codes 0 success / 1 error / 2 auth.
Auto-retries 429 and 5xx up to 3 times, respects Retry-After.
No interactive confirmations - built for agents.
'alpaca api POST /v2/orders' passes raw payloads, enabling MLEG.

nodes.label: alpaca-py / alpaca-trade-api-js
facts: Typed SDKs for Python and JS.
Does NOT satisfy the MCP-or-CLI requirement on its own.

nodes.label: alpaca-skills
facts: Drop-in SKILL.md files for coding agents; npx skills add alpacahq/alpaca-skills
4 Trading-API skills relevant; 10 Broker-API skills are not.
Development aid, not a runtime component.

nodes.label: ALPACA_TOOLSETS
facts: Comma-separated allow-list of MCP toolsets.
Omitting 'trading' makes the LLM structurally incapable of placing an order.
Values: account, trading, watchlists, assets, stock-data, crypto-data, options-data, corporate-actions, news, fixed-income-data, index-data, locates.

nodes.label: Paper environment
facts: New accounts start at $100,000 by default.
Changing the balance requires opening a NEW paper account from the dashboard.
Account number shown upper-left in the dashboard.
Options enabled by default.
Does not simulate market impact, queue position, price improvement, fees, dividends, borrow, slippage or latency.
Injects random partial fills roughly 10% of the time when an order is eligible to fill.

nodes.label: Options Level 3
facts: Level 1 covered calls + cash-secured puts; Level 2 adds long calls/puts; Level 3 adds call and put spreads.
Enabled by default in the paper environment.

nodes.label: MLEG multi-leg orders
facts: order_class: 'mleg' with a legs[] array.
Leg fields: symbol, ratio_qty, side, position_intent.
ratio_qty values must have GCD 1.
Documented strategies: long call spread, long put spread, iron condor, rolls.

nodes.label: No equity legs in MLEG
facts: 'MLeg orders that include an equity leg are not supported.'
Covered calls and collars cannot be a single MLEG order.

nodes.label: All legs covered in-order
facts: 'An MLeg order is accepted only if all its legs are covered within the same MLeg order.'
No naked short legs.

nodes.label: MLEG limit + day only
facts: Every documented example uses type=limit and time_in_force=day.
Market MLEG orders are undocumented - do not assume support.
Consequence: an unfilled spread silently expires at the close.

nodes.label: Universal spread rule
facts: Maintenance margin = max theoretical loss across underlying prices, ignoring premium.
Multiple expirations computed separately; largest requirement applies.
Cost basis = maintenance margin + (net premium x 100).

nodes.label: Auto-exercise and NTA lag
facts: Contracts at least $0.01 ITM are auto-exercised at expiry.
Without buying power, Alpaca sells the position within one hour before expiry.
On paper, non-trade activities sync at the start of the FOLLOWING day.

nodes.label: OCC option symbol
facts: Format: underlying + YYMMDD + C/P + strike x 1000 zero-padded to 8 digits.

nodes.label: Basic plan (free)
facts: Stocks: IEX feed only.
Latest 15 minutes of data withheld.
200 REST requests per minute.
30 stock websocket symbol subscriptions.
Options: indicative feed, 200 quote websocket subscriptions.
Option history available since February 2024.

nodes.label: Algo Trader Plus ($99/mo)
facts: Full SIP stock feed and OPRA options feed.
10,000 requests per minute, unlimited websocket subscriptions.
Awarded as a 1-month subscription to social-engagement prize winners.

nodes.label: Indicative options feed
facts: 'A free derivative of the original OPRA feed: the quotes are not actual OPRA quotes, they're just indicative derivatives. The trades are also derivatives and they're delayed by 15 minutes.'
The feed parameter defaults to opra if subscribed, otherwise indicative - so you get it silently.

nodes.label: Greeks + IV on the free feed
facts: Option snapshot and chain responses include a required greeks object (delta, gamma, theta, vega, rho).
impliedVolatility is computed by Alpaca using Black-Scholes.
Available on the indicative feed - no subscription required.
Derived from indicative quotes: use as a ranking signal, not a pricing oracle.

nodes.label: Option chain endpoint
facts: GET /v1beta1/options/snapshots/{underlying_symbol}
Filters: feed, type, strike_price_gte/lte, expiration_date, expiration_date_gte/lte, root_symbol, updated_since, limit (1-1000), page_token.
Snapshot-by-symbols caps at 100 contracts per request.

nodes.label: Options websocket
facts: wss://stream.data.alpaca.markets/v1beta1/{indicative|opra}
msgpack format only.
Channels: trades (t) and quotes (q) only - no Greeks over the stream.
Cannot subscribe to '*' for option quotes.

nodes.label: Random partial fills on paper
facts: 'When orders are eligible to be filled, they will receive partial fills for a random size 10% of the time.'
On a multi-leg order this leaves a broken, directionally exposed position rather than the intended defined-risk structure.

nodes.label: client_order_id idempotency
facts: Caller-supplied UUID prevents duplicate submission on retry.
Retrievable via GET /v2/orders:by_client_order_id.
Without it, an autonomous agent retrying on network error will eventually double its position.

nodes.label: RULE: autonomous agent
facts: Participants must build autonomous AI trading agents using Alpaca's Trading API.

nodes.label: RULE: MCP or CLI
facts: Projects must utilise either Alpaca's MCP server or its CLI tools.

nodes.label: RULE: options in all strategies
facts: All strategies must incorporate options trading.

nodes.label: RULE: fresh $100k paper account
facts: Final submission must use a brand-new paper account created for the hackathon.
'Projects run on an existing or reused account will not be eligible for judging.'
Starting balance must be $100,000.
The account ID must be submitted so judges can evaluate P&L.

nodes.label: Deadline 4 Sep 2026 15:00 UTC
facts: Kick-off 28 Aug 2026; submissions close 4 Sep 2026 at 15:00 UTC / 20:30 IST.
Roughly 3.5 US market sessions remain as of 1 Sep: 1, 2, 3 Sep full and 90 minutes on 4 Sep.
No market holiday falls in the window - Labor Day 2026 is 7 Sep.

nodes.label: Judging criteria
facts: P&L Performance, Technology Implementation, Creativity & Originality, Presentation & Execution, Social engagement.
No weights are published.
Judges include Alpaca's Trading API team lead and Chief Brokerage Officer.

nodes.label: Featherless AI
facts: Sole named technology partner; serverless open-source model inference.
$25 credits per participant, first-come first-served.
OpenAI-compatible at https://api.featherless.ai/v1 with Bearer auth.
Model families: GLM 5.2, DeepSeek 4, Qwen 3.6, Gemma 4.
1st place carries an extra $300 in Featherless credits.
Partner prizes require the partner tech to be integrated in the submission.

nodes.label: Alpaca's multi-agent reference architecture
facts: 5 isolated research agents (Momentum, Macro, StatArb, Contrarian, Exotic) -> Critic -> human gate -> deterministic Risk Guard -> execution -> 15-min position monitor.
Custom async Python; no LangGraph or CrewAI.
Single SQLite market_snapshot table is the sole agent data interface.
One batch OHLCV request for ~500 tickers avoids rate limits.
Limits: 10% single position, 30% sector, 1.0x leverage, 5/10/15% drawdown halts.
Reported 82 proposals, 26 approved - a 32% approval rate.
GAPS: equities-only and human-gated, so invalid as a hackathon submission as-is.

nodes.label: 'LLM proposes, code disposes'
facts: Adopted independently by roughly two-thirds of the field.
LLM generates or selects; deterministic non-LLM code validates; gates can veto or shrink but never enlarge; every decision including refusals is logged; structures are defined-risk.
TABLE STAKES - build it, but do not lead with it.

nodes.label: Cluster: governance / audit (~15)
facts: Vetoed, Aegis, Horizon Blackline, Visheshak, BABIL, AEGIS-Q, EdgeStack, AegisAlpha x2, TradeMind, Vermilion, SPY Sentinel, Pin Desk.
SATURATED.
Three teams independently chose Aegis-like names.

nodes.label: Cluster: multi-agent debate (~6)
facts: TradeCouncil, Debatte, OptionFlow Sentinel, AlphaSwarm Sovereign, AegisAlpha/Zenith, ORACLE.
CROWDED. Bull/bear + arbiter is the most reused topology.
Debatte's variation - separated data views per analyst - is the most interesting.

nodes.label: Cluster: premium selling / IV (~6)
facts: IV Rank Premium Harvester, VRP Engine, ThetaTrap, Pin Desk, Strike Sentry, Options Sniper.
Economically defensible but theta collection over 3.5 sessions is tiny.

nodes.label: Cluster: news / sentiment (~4)
facts: NewsFlow Trader, Crowd Excess, SOGNO, Strike Sentry.

nodes.label: Cluster: research loops (~3)
facts: Futarchists Options (strategies as genetic sequences), Odysseus (hypothesis -> C# StockSharp -> backtest -> out-of-sample), a continual learning agent.
THIN relative to how impressive it is.

nodes.label: Cluster: portfolio / hedging (~3)
facts: VibeHedge, ORACLE, Vega.
Vega buys convexity while the field sells premium - the contrarian trade of the hackathon.

nodes.label: Cluster: weak / non-compliant (~4)
facts: AI Stock Trading Agent (no options), Cloudrise (no Alpaca tag), KRAKN.AI (options unclear), Tissulogic (thesis is a stretch).
Effective field is closer to ~35 than 41.

nodes.label: OPENING: portfolio-level Greeks
facts: Almost everyone gates per trade; only ORACLE and VibeHedge manage exposure across positions.
Free Greeks make aggregate delta/vega/theta budgeting computable at zero cost.

nodes.label: OPENING: honest feed + fill modelling
facts: No submission summary mentions the indicative feed or random partial fills.
Two Alpaca platform engineers are judging - showing you know indicative != OPRA is instant credibility.

nodes.label: OPENING: closed-loop strategy evolution
facts: Only two or three teams built a system that improves its own strategy.
Impressive on video and independent of live P&L luck.

nodes.label: OPENING: execution quality
facts: Everyone focuses on what to trade; almost nobody on getting filled.
MLEG is limit+day, so non-fills are a real and demonstrable failure mode.

nodes.label: P&L is statistically noise
facts: Only ~3.5 market sessions of judged trading.
Four of five judging criteria are artefact-based and fully controllable.
Bounded, explainable results beat an unexplainable large number - and beat a crater.
